queries: WITH t AS (SELECT p.throws AS hand, COUNT(*) AS n FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY p.throws), s AS (SELECT hand, n, 1.0 * n / SUM(n) OVER () AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT hand, n, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(n) AS combined_tally, AVG(share) AS avg_share_of_selected_hands, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Each manager_award row counts as one award winner, so tied awards each count and a player with several awards counts several times. The inner join to player drops unmatched rows. NULL throws forms its own group.

The average share is the plain mean of the per-hand shares across all hand groups, including the missing group. It is not weighted. 'Their average share' is the mean share of only the above-average hands. The excess is the mean of (hand share minus overall average share) over those hands.

assumptions.assumption: Each manager_award row is one winner (tied awards are separate rows), so the tally counts rows. player_id is unique in player, so the join does not duplicate rows.

The 'average share' is the unweighted mean of the shares across all throwing-hand groups, including the missing (NULL) group. That mean is 1/number of groups. The output's average share is the mean share of the above-average hands, and the excess is the mean of (share minus the average share) over those hands.

responses.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT p.throws AS hand, COUNT(*) AS c FROM manager_award m JOIN player p ON p.player_id = m.player_id GROUP BY p.throws), s AS (SELECT hand, c, c * 1.0 / SUM(c) OVER () AS sh FROM t), a AS (SELECT hand, c, sh, AVG(sh) OVER () AS av FROM s) SELECT SUM(c) AS combined_tally, AVG(sh) AS avg_share, AVG(sh - av) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM a WHERE sh > av

assumptions.assumption: The tally is the number of manager_award rows per throws value. Tied awards count as separate rows. NULL throws forms its own 'missing' group. Rows with no matching player are dropped by the inner join.
The 'average share' is the unweighted mean of the shares across all hand groups, including the missing group. Because the shares sum to 1, this equals 1 divided by the number of groups.
'Their average share' is the mean share of the above-average hands. 'How far above on average' is the mean of (hand share minus the overall average share) across those hands.
player_id is unique in player, so the join does not duplicate award rows.
